idiom_name: Play filters: Filter / EssentialFilter collected by HttpFilters
implementation_notes: Play's filter API is the framework-level realization: a Filter is a curried function nextFilter => requestHeader => Future[Result], the EssentialFilter form wraps EssentialAction when the body must be inspected, and an HttpFilters implementation collects the chain at boot (Play then applies it after routing). The classic Interceptor/Dispatcher/Context trio is replaced by the filter chain plus RequestHeader/Result as the context, and the Scala-idiomatic part is that the interceptor is a function rather than a class - a Function value satisfies the Filter trait by its apply. Hand-written dispatchers remain justified for non-HTTP events (actor extensions, Pekko Streams stages) where no filter contract exists.
pitfalls: Filters wrap the action after the router has picked it, so they cannot influence routing by rewriting path/method/query - that requires an HttpRequestHandler instead.
A filter that returns a Future without invoking next short-circuits every remaining filter and the action, silently; there is no compiler help here.
The implicit ExecutionContext/Materializer must be in scope (and not the global one) or the chain deadlocks under load; ordering is only the order in the HttpFilters sequence.
EssentialFilter gives access to the Accumulator/body - consuming it twice or mapping it after streaming has started fails at run time.
